title: Migrate SCADA Operational Data Feeds to Event-Driven Architecture
narrative: FEDC's SCADA systems generate continuous telemetry from substations, distribution network sensors, and smart meters. This data is currently polled from SCADA systems on fixed 15-minute intervals by the operational data warehouse. The polling approach introduces significant latency for fault detection and means that anomaly data is only visible to operations teams after a delay. Network outages and equipment failures are therefore often detected by field teams or customers before they appear in monitoring dashboards. We propose migrating SCADA operational data feeds to an event-driven architecture using a streaming platform. SCADA systems will publish events at the point of measurement. Subscribing systems — fault management, operations dashboards, predictive maintenance — will consume events in near real time. This reduces fault detection latency from 15 minutes to under 60 seconds and enables proactive rather than reactive operations.

requirements.title: Near real-time delivery
requirements.description: SCADA telemetry events must be available to subscribing systems within 60 seconds of generation under normal operating conditions.

requirements.title: Guaranteed delivery
requirements.description: The streaming platform must guarantee at-least-once delivery of events. Event consumers must handle idempotent processing.

requirements.title: Event schema governance
requirements.description: All SCADA event types must be registered in the integration catalogue with a versioned schema before being published to the streaming platform.
